clue.text: Repeatedly nick steps

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us to write the synonym for nick twice in a row

parts.note: nick and can are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: A petty thief keeps stealing, step after step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' reads as steal, but here it is the noun meaning prison, as is CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively dance, so its high kicks are steps in the dance sense.

clue.text: Old poet's writing, say, after seeing two churches lined with gold

indicators.note: the letter for writing comes after the lined churches
the two church abbreviations are lined with gold, holding it between them

parts.note: CH and CE are both abbreviations for church (CE being Church of England)
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
writing is one of the three Rs, so R stands for it

explanation.surface: A medieval poet's manuscript is read after a tour of two gilded churches.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so 'writing, say' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Chaucer, author of The Canterbury Tales, is a fourteenth-century English poet.

clue.text: Period at sea once, with books welcome on board

indicators.note: the books and welcome go aboard the jumbled letters, sitting inside them
at sea means confused, so the letters of once are jumbled

parts.note: LIT is short for literature, books
hi is a word of welcome

explanation.surface: A time once spent at sea, with books and a warm welcome on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns ONCE into NEOC; 'on board' puts LITHI between its O and C.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic is the New Stone Age, a period of prehistory.

clue.text: After father picked up, see doctor's self-confidence

indicators.note: the remaining pieces follow the lifted father
in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the word for father reads upwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
lo is an old exclamation meaning see or behold
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: After Dad is collected, a visit to the GP restores someone's self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns PA into AP, reading upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is poise and assurance, a cool self-confidence under pressure.

clue.text: Old pile passed on and acquired easily

parts.note: nap is the raised pile on cloth such as velvet
the late means the dead, those who have passed on

explanation.surface: An old heap of property inherited and gained without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile' looks like a fortune or heap, but it is the fluffy surface of a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handed to you on a plate is gained with no effort, an idiom for easy acquisition.

clue.text: Final Tyneside races

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
the TT (Tourist Trophy) are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: The last of the races held on Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nett figure is the final amount left after all deductions, a synonym sense.

clue.text: In The Crown, it's nice playing game on one's own

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go in the word for crown

parts.note: the pate is the crown of the head

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of nice are in play, moved about

explanation.surface: A viewer finds watching the TV drama The Crown a pleasant solitary pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Crown' suggests the Netflix series about the royals; here it is the top of the head. 'playing' scrambles nice to IENC.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the card game, called solitaire in the US, played alone.

clue.text: Very pale, like woman at pre- nuptial event

parts.note: as can mean like, as in 'as white as a sheet'
a hen is a woman at a hen party, the bride's night out before the wedding

explanation.surface: A guest at a hen party turns white as a sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is the British name for a bachelorette party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, grey like ash.

clue.text: Take advantage of policeman when losing daughter in "way out"

indicators.note: the shortened policeman sits in the word for way out

parts.note: an exit is a way out

indicators.note: the policeman loses a letter, the one for daughter

parts.note: plod is British slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: A constable cynically uses his daughter's escape for his own ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Plod is the policeman in Enid Blyton's Noddy stories; 'when losing' drops D, leaving PLO.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to use it to your own benefit, often unfairly.

clue.text: Vehicle in space requiring one-off permit around Italian river

indicators.note: the shortened permit goes around the Italian river
one letter comes off the end of the word for permit

parts.note: to allow is to permit
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: A spacecraft needs a special permit to fly over a river in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-off' looks like a single occasion, but it takes one letter off the end of the permit word, leaving ALLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the NASA programme whose spacecraft carried astronauts to the Moon.

clue.text: Con small person to get in drink

indicators.note: the small person gets in, inside, the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A con artist lures a short man into a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch-up is a deception that frames or cheats someone, so it is a con.

clue.text: Rising reserve wins corner in game

indicators.note: wins here means takes in, so the reversed reserve holds the corner
in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: a nook is a corner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' gives SER, read upwards in this down entry; 'wins' is a container signal, not victory.

clue.text: Shaving, brother heard rodent

explanation.definitionFit: The chipmunk is a small striped squirrel of North America, a rodent.

clue.text: Musician's slowly procuring a building alongside house?

parts.note: lento is the musical direction meaning slowly

explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed with a sloping roof built against the wall of a house.

clue.text: Drive back and act like an aristocrat

parts.note: to be something is to act like it, play the part
toff is British slang for a posh, upper-class person

explanation.surface: Repel attackers while behaving like a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a three-word phrase about behaving like a posh person; run together it means repel.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat off attackers is to repel or drive them back.

clue.text: Some commuter hurried around industrial region

indicators.note: around signals the hidden letters are turned round
some of the letters across the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A hurried commuter dashes about an industrial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes RHUR from commuteR HURried; 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is Germany's great coal and steel area, a classic industrial region.

clue.text: East Sussex resident maybe caught aquatic transport — and another type

parts.note: a whimsical name for someone from Hove, a seaside town in East Sussex

a raft is a simple craft for travel on water

explanation.surface: A local from the south coast is spotted aboard a raft and another vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a town beside Brighton; a 'Hover' is a playful coinage for one of its residents. 'another type' refers back to the raft, defining by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovercraft rides on a cushion of air over water, a further kind of watercraft beside the raft.

clue.text: Vegetable outstanding soldier keeps in pannier regularly

explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of pannier; a pannier is a bag slung on a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine, called eggplant in America, is a purple vegetable.

clue.text: Vehicle with A-reg vacated in the ancient city

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the emptied letters go in the word the
vacated means emptied of the middle, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: An old car with an A-registration plate is abandoned in the old town.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-reg is a British number plate from 1983-84; 'vacated' leaves AG.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the ancient Phoenician city in North Africa destroyed by Rome.

clue.text: Perhaps wedding ring found somewhere in California

parts.note: marriage is one of the Christian sacraments, so a wedding is an example of one
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A wedding ring discovered somewhere in the Golden State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like part of the wedding, but it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Bird rolls about in mud perhaps, tail first

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is moved to the front

parts.note: an animal that wallows rolls around in mud or water

explanation.surface: A bird flops about in the mud, tail end leading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail first' moves the last S of WALLOWS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallow is a fork-tailed migratory songbird.

clue.text: Competent learner sitting in Lincoln

indicators.note: the learner sits inside the name

parts.note: Abe was the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' suggests the English city; it is the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means having the skill to do something, a synonym of competent.

clue.text: The day before holiday peak

parts.note: an eve is the day before a festival, as in Christmas Eve
rest is a break, a holiday from work

explanation.surface: The day before a holiday is the high point.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain, a peak in the Himalaya.

clue.text: Bobby, I'm surprised, embraces social science course

clue.text: Pump up a cycle — flat tyre, at rear

clue.text: Anyone raging repeatedly inside needs this spiritualist?
